The evidence is conclusive:

**Key observations:**
- Image shows loose corn kernels photographed under UV/black light (dark background, purple-blue ambient glow)
- Several kernels exhibit intense bright green-cyan fluorescence
- This is the classic **BGYF (Bright Greenish-Yellow Fluorescence)** test — the standard diagnostic for *Aspergillus flavus* aflatoxin contamination in corn
- No other corn disease produces this UV fluorescence signature

**Ruling out alternatives:**
- Fusarium: white/pink mycelium on ear, no UV fluorescence
- Trichoderma: teal-green mold visible in daylight, not UV
- Diplodia: white mold, white kernels, no UV glow
- Gibberella: pink/red mycelium, no UV fluorescence
- All leaf diseases (Gray leaf spot, NCLB, rusts, etc.) are irrelevant — this is ear/kernel tissue

The UV fluorescence test is pathognomonic for Aspergillus ear rot. This image is a textbook example of the BGYF diagnostic.
